title.narrative: Integrated Life-Saving Response for Internally Displaced Populations in the Informal Settlements of Kersadula and Deka Suftu Woredas, Liben Zone, Somali Region, Ethiopia.

description.narrative: ltpgtEthiopia’s Somali Region continues to experience a humanitarian crisis driven by conflict, climate shocks, and displacement. In Liben Zone alone, over 40,000 IDPs reside in informal settlements, with Kersadula and DekaSuftu woredas hosting some of the highest concentrations. Most HHs have minimal access to basic services. Joint assessments conducted by PAPDA, in collaboration with local authorities and humanitarian actors, covered all IDP HHs, averaging 7–8 members each. Findings confirmed Nutrition/Food (100%), Health (93%), and WASH (86%) as the most urgent needs. Families have exhausted all coping mechanisms, lacking income, assets, or savings, and are entirely dependent on humanitarian assistance for survival. Health services are critically overstretched: facilities are often 1–2 hrs away by foot, with limited medicines, insufficient skilled staff, inadequate reproductive health services, and weak outbreak surveillance. WASH conditions are dire: women and girls travel long distances under unsafe conditions to collect water, 74–100% of HHs consume untreated water, and sanitation infrastructure is almost nonexistent. Protection risks remain extremely high, as the absence of safe spaces, reporting mechanisms, and community-based structures exposes women, girls, elderly persons, and persons with disabilities to GBV, exploitation, child marriage, and harmful traditional practices. Since 2006, PAPDA has maintained a strong operational presence in Liben Zone, with coordination offices in Filtu and field bases in Kersadula and DekaSuftu. The organization currently implements complementary programs, including a GAVI-supported U5 vaccination initiative and a peacebuilding project with Brot PADD, demonstrating capacity for rapid response, coordination, and sustained community engagement. This proposed intervention aligns with the EHF 3rd Reserve Allocation Priority 1 and the 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan, targeting 53,863 direct and 150,000 indirect beneficiaries through an integrated multi-sector response across Health, Nutrition, WASH, Protection/GBV, ESNFI, and MPCA with project budget of 1M USD. Health interventions will deploy 2 MHNTs per woreda, providing primary healthcare, MISP, immunizations, emergency referrals, and capacity-building for health workers. Nutrition services will strengthen CMAM, including SAM/MAM treatment, MUAC screening by 1,000 trained caregivers, IYCF counselling, and community cooking demonstrations for 1,600 mothers and caregivers. WASH activities include solar rehabilitation of water systems, construction of communal latrines, hygiene promotion, and distribution of water treatment chemicals, HH NFIs, and menstrual MHM kits. MPCA will reach 500 vulnerable HHs, using market assessments and verified targeting to ensure dignity, choice, and financial protection. Protection and GBV components will screen 4,000 individuals for vulnerability, conduct 5 protection monitoring, and provide GBV case management and PSS. Two women and girls’ safe spaces or mobile points will offer referrals, awareness sessions, and cluster-standard dignity kits to 500 beneficiaries. Six inclusive community protection committees and 2,000 IEC materials will promote protective norms and strengthen community-led approaches. Standard ESNFI kits will be distributed to 1,180 affected IDP HHs. The intervention embeds a strong localization and accountability-to-affected-populations (AAP) framework through partnerships with national women-led organizations: GWEDE(WASH) and MCDO(Protection/GBV), for which PAPDA provides capacity gap identification and institutional capacity strengthening through supportive technical mentoring, training and operational working systems enhancement. The project will collaborate with local government, community representatives, other stakeholders and clusters to ensure accountability, do not harm, PSEA, inclusivity, coordination, sustainability, and long-term support for IDP communities in both woredas.ltbrgtlt/pgt
